clue.text: How a candidate in the Manchester area moved house

definitions.text: How a candidate in the Manchester area moved house

parts.words: How a candidate in the Manchester area moved house
parts.note: a candidate is put up (nominated) to stand for Sale, a town in Greater Manchester; the same phrase describes offering a home to buyers when moving

explanation.surface: A political hopeful in the north-west relocates during the campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: Sale is a town in the Manchester area, so a candidate there is put up for Sale; read as one phrase, it is what you do with your home before you move.
explanation.definitionFit: Before moving, a householder lists the property with an estate agent, offering it to buyers.

clue.text: Father's enclosing heath with fencing stakes

indicators.note: enclosing tells us the father's word wraps around the word for heath

parts.note: Father is PA, and the 's adds an S
ling is heather, the plant of heathland

explanation.surface: A dad has fenced off a stretch of moorland with posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pales are pointed wooden posts that make up a fence.

clue.text: Pair of Warrant Officers immersed in a big book

indicators.note: immersed in means the officers' letters sit inside the book's word

parts.note: a tome is a large, heavy book
WO is the military abbreviation for Warrant Officer; plural WOS

explanation.surface: Two army officers are absorbed in reading a huge volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple of people together form a duo.

clue.text: It records how far Walker (MP) goes around a cupola

indicators.note: goes around shows the politician's first name encircles the word for cupola

parts.note: Peter Walker was a Conservative MP and cabinet minister
a cupola is a dome on a roof

explanation.surface: A politician's stroll around a domed building is being measured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walker' looks like part of the definition (a gadget for walkers) but is the MP Peter Walker, a British Conservative cabinet minister.
explanation.definitionFit: This device counts steps to measure the distance a person walks.

clue.text: Convenient place to hang the bath plug?

definitions.text: Convenient place to hang the bath plug?

parts.words: Convenient place to hang the bath plug?
parts.note: a plug on its chain may be hung over a faucet; the phrase also means readily available

explanation.surface: Where should you keep the stopper for the tub?
explanation.definitionFit: Something readily available for use is described by this phrase, as with draught beer.

clue.text: Informed on what the customer did

definitions.meaning: betrayed someone to the police, slang
a customer went round the stores buying things

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for reporting someone to the authorities, and also the past of going round stores.

clue.text: Knocked unconscious and prepared for burial

definitions.meaning: a corpse is arranged and dressed before a funeral

explanation.definitionFit: A boxer floored cold and a corpse arranged for viewing are both described by this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Call in at once in order to secure a last-minute booking

indicators.note: in order asks for the letters of the first words to be put into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Phone straight away to grab a late reservation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' reads as part of 'in order to', but it is the anagram signal on CALL IN AT ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: When someone else withdraws a reservation, a late place opens up for a new customer.

clue.text: Everything considered, no one has been left in the dark

definitions.text: no one has been left in the dark

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in total, and read literally says every person has been informed.

clue.text: All an American has to rub together if he tears his dollar in half?

definitions.text: All an American has to rub together if he tears his dollar in half?

parts.words: All an American has to rub together if he tears his dollar in half?
parts.note: an American slang term for a quarter of a dollar; a dollar torn in half literally leaves a couple of pieces

explanation.surface: A broke American rips his only banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: In US slang a 'bit' is 12.5 cents, so the phrase means 25 cents, a trifling sum.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for a quarter, and by extension a trifling sum.

clue.text: What a disciplinarian captain takes to ascertain the size of his poop

definitions.text: What a disciplinarian captain takes to ascertain the size of his poop

parts.words: What a disciplinarian captain takes to ascertain the size of his poop
parts.note: a harsh step a strict captain imposes; also a gauging of the rear of his ship, the poop being the raised rear deck

explanation.surface: A strict ship's master sizes up the rear deck of his vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The poop is the raised deck at the back of a ship, the rear end being its stern.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh disciplinary step is a severe action, and literally a gauging of the back of a ship.

clue.text: Study class has to do the accepted thing

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A school class is told to behave properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply with social norms is to follow convention.

clue.text: So a pope managed to be a little brave

indicators.note: managed suggests the letters are handled and rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Thus a pontiff found the courage for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: a young Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American baby, carried on the back, is a tiny warrior-to-be.

clue.text: Dull yarn describing large romantic island

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothes labels
isle is the poetic or romantic word for island

explanation.surface: A boring story set on a dreamy island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' suggests a tale but is thread: a strong cotton thread used for stockings, matt rather than shiny like silk.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard-twisted cotton thread, used for stockings, without the sheen of silk.

clue.text: Took dress into fitting-room and attempted to get away with it

definitions.meaning: put on a garment in a shop to check the fit

definitions.text: attempted to get away with it
definitions.meaning: chanced one's luck at a deception

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means put a garment on for size, and colloquially chanced a deception.

clue.text: Redundant workers for whom Satan finds mischief

definitions.meaning: from the proverb that the devil finds work for the unoccupied

explanation.definitionFit: Unoccupied labourers, and the subject of the proverb about the devil finding work for them.

clue.text: Related to the family originating from Lancaster

indicators.note: originating from says the answer is made out of the letters of the city name, rearranged

explanation.surface: A family whose roots lie in the northern city of Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancaster is a city in north-west England, also the royal house of Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Inherited or descended from forebears, belonging to one's lineage.

clue.text: Get a cot made for a little house

indicators.note: made says the letters are fashioned into something new

explanation.surface: Buy a crib for a small home.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rural dwelling, typically in the country.

clue.text: A wild hitter but a hard worker

definitions.meaning: a batsman or boxer who swings hard without finesse

explanation.definitionFit: Both a batsman who swipes wildly and a person who toils away are described by this noun.

clue.text: Stuff a pancake

definitions.meaning: a crinkled fabric, stuff meaning material

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a crinkled fabric and also a thin French pancake.

clue.text: A holy man entering a miracle town for a game of cards

indicators.note: entering shows the holy man pieces go inside the town's name

parts.note: Cana in Galilee, where Jesus turned water into wine
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A saint arrives at a Biblical town to play bridge or rummy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rummy-style card game from South America played with two packs.

clue.text: Use evil machination which is difficult to pin down

indicators.note: machination, a scheming manipulation, signals the letters being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A villain's plot that cannot be traced.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hard to catch or define slips away from grasp.

clue.text: Short introduction to Italian anthem

parts.note: intro is the shortened form of introduction

explanation.surface: Opening bars of a national song from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalm or chant sung as the priest approaches the altar at the start of Mass.

clue.text: Turned Rex out despite being well-tempered

indicators.note: out means the king's letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: Rex is Latin for king, abbreviated R

explanation.surface: A king was expelled yet stayed calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-tempered' suggests calm, but it is the musical sense of instruments adjusted to pitch, as in Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruments adjusted to correct pitch are said to be well-tempered.

clue.text: Small number put in lots of time to obtain good degree

indicators.note: put in shows the number's abbreviation goes inside the time word

parts.note: hours are a lot of time
No is the shortened form of number

explanation.surface: A student spends hours working for a first-class result.
explanation.walkthrough: A British university degree with distinction beyond a pass is called an honours degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A university degree of higher standard than an ordinary pass.

clue.text: Cattle trap was "mother's ruin"

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, as in neatsfoot oil
a gin is a snare for animals

explanation.surface: Getting caught in a snare by livestock was mum's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother's ruin' is British slang for gin, from its notoriety in the 18th century; here the spirit is taken undiluted.
explanation.definitionFit: The juniper spirit got this slang nickname, here drunk without mixer.

clue.text: Less pleasant Stainer composition

indicators.note: composition suggests the name's letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A piece by the composer John Stainer that is rather unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: John Stainer was a Victorian English composer, so 'composition' looks like one of his works.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning unpleasant or mean.

clue.text: Surrounding Diana with pansies could give one palpitations

indicators.note: Surrounding tells us the flower name goes around the short name for Diana

parts.note: heartsease is the wild pansy
Di is the short form of Diana

explanation.surface: A bouquet of flowers around Diana sets her pulse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardiac condition may cause an irregular, racing pulse.
